title: Yakgwa Honey-Ginger Cookies
shortDescription: Fluted honey-ginger cookies are fried slowly, drained, and soaked in a warm aromatic honey syrup.
culturalContext: Yakgwa is a traditional Korean confection associated with celebrations and tea tables. Shapes, frying sequences, grain syrups, honey, spices, and garnish vary; this draft omits alcohol and requires cultural and test-kitchen review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

instructions.heading: Cook the syrup
instructions.action: Simmer syrup honey, water, and ginger for 5 minutes; remove from heat and cool to warm.
instructions.safetyNote: Hot honey syrup causes severe burns; keep handles inward and do not taste while hot.

instructions.heading: Make the dough
instructions.action: Whisk flour and cinnamon, rub in sesame oil, then fold in honey, water, and ginger just until a dough forms.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Dough holds together without being kneaded smooth.
instructions.safetyNote: Raw flour can contain germs; do not taste raw dough and clean flour dust promptly.

instructions.heading: Shape and vent
instructions.action: Roll 12 mm / 1/2 inch thick, cut 18 pieces, and pierce each center several times.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are even and perforated through the center.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw dough away from ready-to-eat food.

instructions.heading: Fry in batches
instructions.action: Heat oil in a deep pot and fry small batches, turning gently, until deep golden and cooked through.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cookies are evenly deep golden and bubbles slow.
instructions.safetyNote: Never leave hot oil unattended; keep water away, avoid crowding, and use a thermometer.

instructions.heading: Drain safely
instructions.action: Lift cookies with a spider and drain on a rack for 2 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Excess oil drains and cookies remain intact.
instructions.safetyNote: Cookies and oil remain hot; cool frying oil fully before moving or disposal.

instructions.heading: Soak and set
instructions.action: Place warm cookies in warm syrup, turn to coat, soak 2 hours, then drain before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cookies are glossy and syrup has penetrated the crumb.
instructions.safetyNote: Use heat-safe utensils and cool promptly after soaking.

grillSetup: No grill required; deep-fry only on a stable stovetop with the pot no more than half full and a lid nearby for emergency smothering.
visualDonenessCues: Bubbles slow near the end of frying
Interior is cooked with no raw flour pocket
foodSafetyNotes: Do not eat or taste raw flour or raw dough.
Control oil with a thermometer at 300 to 325°F / 149 to 163°C and never add water to hot oil.
Hot honey syrup can stick to skin and cause severe burns.
Do not extinguish a grease fire with water; turn off heat if safe and smother with a lid.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: A gluten-free version requires separate formulation and validation.
Rice syrup may replace part of the honey only after a test cook.
ingredientSourcing: Use fresh flour stored dry and within its date.
Verify sesame-oil and frying-oil labels for cross-contact.
makeAhead: After cooling, prepare up to 1 day ahead.
storage: Store covered at cool room temperature for up to 1 day or refrigerate up to 3 days pending test-kitchen validation.
reheating: Serve at room temperature; do not microwave syrup-coated cookies to a dangerously hot center.
leftovers: Discard cookies handled by diners or left exposed to contamination; cool and cover clean leftovers.
servingSuggestions: Serve one small cookie with unsweetened tea.
Cut for diners who need smaller portions.

faq.question: Can I taste the dough?
faq.answer: No. Flour is raw until cooked and should not be tasted.

faq.question: Why use a thermometer?
faq.answer: Frying-temperature control reduces scorching, oil overflow, and undercooked centers.
